Summary of the 8-K filed May 1, 2026. Cited figures are marked; the original filing is the authoritative source.
Church & Dwight (CHD) reported first-quarter 2026 results that beat its own outlook on sales, gross margin and adjusted EPS, while reiterating full-year 2026 guidance.
Reported net sales rose 0.2% to $1,469.3 million a , but the company stresses that this figure is flattered by the 2025 strategic portfolio actions (divestitures such as VMS), which subtracted 8.1% from growth. Organic sales grew 5.0% (versus a 3% outlook), driven by 5.3% volume growth, with all three divisions growing: Consumer Domestic + 5.4% , Consumer International + 3.7% , and Specialty Products + 3.1% . Reported EPS was $0.91 (vs. $0.89 ) and adjusted EPS was $0.95 , up 4.4% , against a company outlook of $0.92 .
Adjusted gross margin expanded 130 bps to 46.4% , helped by volume, productivity and mix, partly offset by inflation and tariffs. Profitability was more mixed. Marketing spend rose and adjusted SG&A climbed 110 bps as a share of sales, driven by the TOUCHLAND acquisition's amortization and SG&A, so adjusted operating income was essentially flat at $302.6 million b .
Operating cash flow fell $10.9 million to $174.8 million c on higher working capital, and capex nearly doubled to $31.9 million . Cash rose to $503.4 million against $2.2 billion of total debt. Full-year 2026 guidance was reiterated: organic growth of 3% to 4% , reported sales down 1.5% to 0.5% due entirely to 2025 portfolio exits, reported EPS up 18% to 22% , adjusted EPS up 5% to 8% , and operating cash flow of about $1.15 billion .
Management flagged the Middle East situation as a source of incremental volume and inflationary pressure on commodities and transportation, which it expects to offset. The Q2 outlook calls for adjusted EPS of $0.88 d , with EPS growth weighted to the second half.
